name: Desire and anger, the enemy (kāma–krodha)
description: Desire, and anger with it, born of rajas, all-devouring, is the constant enemy of the wise; it covers knowledge as smoke covers fire and has the senses, mind and intellect as its seat (BhG 3.36–43).
antidotes: knowing the self beyond the intellect (3.43)

name: The three gates of hell: desire, anger, greed
description: Desire, anger and greed are the threefold gate of hell, destructive of the self, to be abandoned (BhG 16.21–22).

name: The chain of ruin from dwelling on objects
description: Dwelling on objects breeds attachment; attachment desire; desire anger; anger delusion; delusion loss of memory; loss of memory destruction of the intellect; and so one perishes (BhG 2.62–63).
antidotes: moving among objects free of attraction and aversion (2.64)

name: The turbulent senses
description: The senses are turbulent and carry off the mind even of a striving wise man, as the wind carries off a ship (BhG 2.60, 2.67); attraction and aversion lurk in each sense (3.34).

name: The restless mind
description: The mind is restless, turbulent, strong and obstinate, as hard to restrain as the wind (BhG 6.34); it wanders from the object of meditation (6.26).

name: Despondency (viṣāda)
description: Arjuna's grief and dejection on seeing his kinsmen — trembling, dry mouth, failing limbs, confusion about dharma, faint-heartedness (kārpaṇya) — which moves him to lay down his bow (BhG 1.28–47; 2.1–7).
antidotes: the teacher's instruction on the self and on svadharma (2.11–38)

name: Delusion (moha)
description: Delusion, born of anger (BhG 2.63) and of the pairs of opposites (7.27), by which the world does not know the Lord (7.13); destroyed by knowledge and grace (4.35; 18.73).
notes: U05's contribution to a shared obstacle.

name: Ignorance veiling knowledge (ajñāna)
description: Knowledge is veiled by ignorance, by which beings are deluded (BhG 5.15); the ignorant, faithless doubter perishes (4.40); tamas is born of ignorance (14.8).
notes: U05's contribution to a shared obstacle.

name: The sense of 'I am the doer' (kartṛtva-abhimāna)
description: Deluded by ego one thinks 'I am the doer' of actions done by the guṇas of prakṛti (BhG 3.27); one who sees the self alone as agent does not see (18.16).

name: Attachment to the fruits of action (phala-saṅga)
description: The unyoked, attached to the fruit through desire, is bound (BhG 5.12); those whose motive is the fruit are pitiable (2.49).

name: Bondage by the three guṇas
description: The guṇas bind the embodied one: sattva by attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas by attachment to action, tamas by negligence, sloth and sleep (BhG 14.5–8); attachment to the guṇas causes birth in good and evil wombs (13.21).
antidotes: seeing no agent but the guṇas (14.19)
members: sattva: attachment to happiness and knowledge

name: The demonic endowment
description: Hypocrisy, arrogance, pride, anger, harshness and ignorance, leading to bondage (BhG 16.4–5), with its denial of truth, foundation and a Lord and its life for desire (16.8–18).

name: Doubt (saṃśaya)
description: The doubting self perishes; for the doubter there is neither this world nor the next nor happiness (BhG 4.40); doubt born of ignorance is to be cut with the sword of knowledge (4.42).

name: Lack of faith (aśraddhā)
description: Those without faith in this dharma return to the path of death and saṃsāra (BhG 9.3); what is done without faith is 'asat' (17.28); the faithless doubter perishes (4.40).

name: Attachment to the rewards of ritual (vedavāda)
description: Delight in the Vedic words that promise heaven, enjoyment and power keeps the resolute understanding from being established in samādhi (BhG 2.42–44); those who seek heaven by the three Vedas return when their merit is spent (9.20–21).
antidotes: being free of the three guṇas (2.45)

name: The five faults of yoga (Mokṣadharma)
description: Desire, anger, greed, fear and sleep — the five faults of yoga that the seers know, to be cut off (MBh 12.232.4; also 12.266.14).

name: The six faults to be abandoned (Viduranīti)
description: Sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, sloth and procrastination are to be abandoned by one who seeks prosperity (MBh 5.33.66).

name: Craving (tṛṣṇā)
description: Thirst, from which with attachment rajas arises and binds by attachment to action (BhG 14.7).

name: Hope, expectation (āśā)
description: Hope is the great sorrow and freedom from hope the highest happiness, as Piṅgalā learned (MBh 12.168.52).

name: Heedlessness (pramāda)
description: Heedlessness is death (Sanatsujāta, MBh 5.42.4); negligence is a bond of tamas (BhG 14.8).
